es.summary: Pérdida grave de la función hepática que impide la síntesis de proteínas, la detoxificación y la producción de bilis. Puede ser aguda o crónica y se asocia a ictericia, ascitis y encefalopatía.
key_points: Disminución de la síntesis de albúmina y factores de coagulación.
Acumulación de bilirrubina causa ictericia y prurito.
Ascitis y edema reflejan hipertensión portal.
Encefalopatía hepática se presenta con alteración mental.
Laboratorio: AST/ALT elevados, INR >1.5, albúmina <3.5 g/dL.

pathophysiology: Daño hepatocelular reduce síntesis de proteínas plasmáticas.
Obstrucción del flujo portal genera hipertensión portal.
Hipertensión portal produce ascitis y varices esofágicas.
Acumulación de amoníaco y toxinas causa encefalopatía.
Disminución de la detoxificación lleva a hipercalemia y acidosis.
diagnostics: AST, ALT >2‑3 veces límite superior normal.
INR >1.5 y tiempo de protrombina prolongado.
Ecografía hepática: tamaño reducido, nódulos, flujo portal alterado.
treatment: Restricción de sodio <2 g/día y manejo de líquidos.
Diuréticos de asa (furosemida) y espironolactona para ascitis.
Lactulosa y rifaximina para encefalopatía hepática.
Albúmina intravenosa en casos de hipovolemia.
nursing_care: Monitorear signos vitales y nivel de conciencia cada 2‑4 h.
Registrar ingesta y eliminación; objetivo balance hídrico neutro.
Evaluar abdomen: distensión, turgencia, presencia de ascitis.
Controlar peso diario; alerta aumento >2 kg/24 h.
Vigilar electrolitos y coagulación; notificar valores críticos.
patient_teaching: Seguir dieta baja en sodio y evitar alcohol.
Tomar medicamentos según indicación, sin omitir dosis.
Reportar cambios en nivel de conciencia o asterixis.
Acudir a controles de laboratorio y ecografía regularmente.

evidenced_by: aumento de peso >2 kg en 24 h
outcomes: Balance hídrico: mantener ingesta y eliminación dentro de ±500 mL en 24 h
Edema: reducir edema periférico visible en 48 h

interventions.action: Registrar ingesta y eliminación cada 4 h y comparar con objetivo de balance hídrico
interventions.rationale: Permite detectar acumulación de líquidos y ajustar terapia diurética

interventions.action: Elevar extremidades inferiores 30° cuando haya edema
interventions.rationale: Facilita el retorno venoso y disminuye la acumulación intersticial

interventions.action: Administrar diuréticos según prescripción y observar respuesta clínica
interventions.rationale: Promueve la excreción de sodio y agua para reducir ascitis y edema

interventions.action: Aplicar compresión ligera en piernas si no hay contraindicación
interventions.rationale: Ayuda a movilizar el líquido intersticial hacia la circulación

interventions.action: Evaluar abdomen por turgencia y medir circunferencia cada 12 h
interventions.rationale: Monitorea la progresión o mejoría de la ascitis

outcomes: Electrolitos: mantener Na+ 135‑145 mEq/L y K+ 3.5‑5.0 mEq/L

interventions.action: Obtener muestra de sangre para electrolitos cada 24 h
interventions.rationale: Detecta alteraciones tempranas y permite corrección oportuna

interventions.action: Administrar suplementos de potasio o magnesio según orden médica
interventions.rationale: Previene hipocalemia y arritmias asociadas

interventions.action: Educar al paciente sobre alimentos ricos en potasio (plátano, papaya) y limitar diuréticos sin supervisión
interventions.rationale: Promueve autocuidado y evita desequilibrios evitables

interventions.action: Monitorear ECG por cambios de onda T o arritmias cuando se administre furosemida
interventions.rationale: La hipokalemia puede producir alteraciones cardíacas

interventions.action: Registrar signos de neuromuscular (calambres, debilidad) cada turno
interventions.rationale: Indicadores clínicos de desequilibrio electrolítico

en.summary: Severe loss of liver function that impairs protein synthesis, detoxification, and bile production. It can be acute or chronic and is associated with jaundice, ascites, and encephalopathy.
key_points: Decreased synthesis of albumin and clotting factors.
Accumulation of bilirubin causes jaundice and pruritus.
Ascites and edema reflect portal hypertension.
Hepatic encephalopathy presents with altered mental status.
Lab: AST/ALT elevated, INR >1.5, albumin <3.5 g/dL.

pathophysiology: Hepatocellular damage reduces plasma protein synthesis.
Portal flow obstruction generates portal hypertension.
Portal hypertension produces ascites and esophageal varices.
Accumulation of ammonia and toxins causes encephalopathy.
Reduced detoxification leads to hyperkalemia and acidosis.
diagnostics: AST, ALT >2‑3× upper limit of normal.
Abdominal ultrasound: reduced size, nodules, altered portal flow.
treatment: Sodium restriction <2 g/day and fluid management.
Loop diuretics (furosemide) and spironolactone for ascites.
Lactulose and rifaximin for hepatic encephalopathy.
Intravenous albumin in cases of hypovolemia.
nursing_care: Monitor vital signs and level of consciousness every 2‑4 h.
Record intake and output; goal neutral fluid balance.
Assess abdomen: distension, turgor, presence of ascites.
Weigh daily; alert if weight increases >2 kg/24 h.
Monitor electrolytes and coagulation; report critical values.
patient_teaching: Follow a low‑sodium diet and avoid alcohol.
Take medications as prescribed, do not skip doses.
Report changes in level of consciousness or asterixis.
Attend regular lab and ultrasound follow‑ups.

outcomes: Fluid balance: maintain intake and output within ±500 mL in 24 h
Edema: reduce visible peripheral edema within 48 h

interventions.action: Record intake and output every 4 h and compare with fluid balance goal
interventions.rationale: Allows detection of fluid accumulation and adjustment of diuretic therapy

interventions.action: Elevate lower extremities 30° when edema is present
interventions.rationale: Facilitates venous return and reduces interstitial accumulation

interventions.action: Administer diuretics as prescribed and observe clinical response
interventions.rationale: Promotes sodium and water excretion to reduce ascites and edema

interventions.action: Apply light compression to legs if no contraindication
interventions.rationale: Helps mobilize interstitial fluid into circulation

interventions.action: Assess abdomen for turgor and measure circumference every 12 h
interventions.rationale: Monitors progression or improvement of ascites

outcomes: Electrolytes: maintain Na+ 135‑145 mEq/L and K+ 3.5‑5.0 mEq/L

interventions.action: Obtain blood sample for electrolytes every 24 h
interventions.rationale: Detects early changes and allows timely correction

interventions.action: Administer potassium or magnesium supplements as ordered
interventions.rationale: Prevents hypokalemia and associated arrhythmias

interventions.action: Educate patient on potassium‑rich foods (banana, papaya) and limit unsupervised diuretics
interventions.rationale: Promotes self‑care and avoids avoidable imbalances

interventions.action: Monitor ECG for T‑wave changes or arrhythmias when furosemide is given
interventions.rationale: Hypokalemia can cause cardiac alterations

interventions.action: Record neuromuscular signs (cramps, weakness) each shift
interventions.rationale: Clinical indicators of electrolyte imbalance

summary.1.quote: Signs of chronic liver disease may be nonspecific and include anorexia, weight loss, fatigue, ascites, esophageal varices, or jaundice (Sharma & Nagalli, 2023).

key_points.0.quote: Liver function tests may show increased alanine transaminase (ALT) level and aspartate aminotransferase (AST) levels, bilirubin and prothrombin times will be increased, and albumin level decreased.

key_points.2.quote: Without treatment, portal hypertension can cause complications such as variceal bleeding, ascites, hepatorenal syndrome , infection, and cardiomyopathy.

key_points.3.quote: A mental status decline accompanying an increase in ammonia level may indicate hepatic encephalopathy.

sections.pathophysiology.1.quote: Portal Hypertension Another liver condition, portal hypertension , is an increase in pressure within the portal venous system because of resistance to portal blood flow.

sections.pathophysiology.2.quote: Without treatment, portal hypertension can cause complications such as variceal bleeding, ascites, hepatorenal syndrome , infection, and cardiomyopathy.

sections.risk_factors.1.quote: The most common types of viral hepatitis are A, B, C, D, and E.

sections.signs_symptoms.0.quote: Jaundice occurs when skin and sclera (whites of the eyes) ( Figure 19.17 ) turn yellow as a result of too much bilirubin in the body.

sections.signs_symptoms.1.quote: Figure 19.19 Ascites is a condition in which the abdominal cavity fills with fluid that shifts from the intravascular to the interstitial space, resulting in hypovolemia.

sections.signs_symptoms.4.quote: The bleeding at a venipuncture site followed by oozing of blood from every site or orifice available could indicate coagulopathy, such as disseminated intravascular coagulation.

sections.complications.1.quote: Without treatment, portal hypertension can cause complications such as variceal bleeding, ascites, hepatorenal syndrome , infection, and cardiomyopathy.

sections.complications.2.quote: Common complications seen with chronic liver disease are esophageal varices , hepatic encephalopathy, hepatorenal syndrome (kidney dysfunction in patients with advanced liver disease), and hepatocellular carcinoma.

sections.complications.3.quote: The bleeding at a venipuncture site followed by oozing of blood from every site or orifice available could indicate coagulopathy, such as disseminated intravascular coagulation.

sections.patient_teaching.1.quote: Take heart failure medications as prescribed by their health care provider.
